title: One-sided randomized language recognition
statement: Fix a verifier model $E$ and a language $L$ of finite Boolean lists. The language $L$ has an efficient verifier relative to $E$ if there exist a Boolean-valued verifier $M$ and natural numbers $a,k$ such that the optional-output verifier associated with $M$ is efficient according to $E$, and for every Boolean list $x$, membership in $L$ implies that $M$ accepts with probability at least $2/3$ when given a uniformly random string of length $ igl(	ext{polyLen}(a,k,|x|) igr)$, while nonmembership implies that $M$ rejects for every random string of that length.
hypotheses_covered: A language $L$ of finite Boolean lists
There exist a Boolean-valued verifier $M$ and natural numbers $a,k$
The optional-output verifier associated with $M$ is efficient according to $E$
For every Boolean list $x$, if $x\in L$, acceptance probability at the specified random-bit length is at least $2/3$
For every Boolean list $x$, if $x\notin L$, every random string of the specified length is rejected
